text:
Gabriel Landeskog scored twice, and Colorado used the final stretch of a tied game to bury a Toronto team that is now winless in four (0-4-0). The Leafs had answered Landeskog's second goal, a backhand just 51 seconds after Jack Roslovic tied it 3-3 early in the third. Then Artturi Lehkonen and Martin Necas scored 15 seconds apart late, and Colorado walked off with a 6-3 win in a building where Toronto had beaten them 6-3 a month earlier.

Landeskog was drafted second overall by the Avalanche in 2011 out of Kitchener, and this was a night when he looked the part, with four shots on goal and 1.75 expected goals (a measure of chance quality) for Colorado while he was on the ice, against 0.49 for Toronto. By that measure Colorado had the better of it, 3.65 to 2.49 overall, and our simulation of every shot gives the Avalanche a 61% chance of winning a replay. But the gap wasn't as wide as the score. At even strength the two sides were nearly level (2.58 to 2.47), and Toronto had more shot attempts, 62 to 59. Colorado's edge came mostly in the third period, 1.69 to 0.98.

The goaltending tilted it further. Sergei Bobrovsky allowed 1.9 more goals than the shots he faced should have produced, while Mackenzie Blackwood was slightly worse than expected (0.5 goals) and still stopped Roslovic on a 21% chance in the third. Darren Raddysh's opener came on a chance worth under 1%. For Toronto, the four-game winless run continues. Colorado, with the win, has now split the season series with the Leafs.
